learning.initial: For a classroom exercise, give sensitivity and specificity for a fictional screening dataset: 30 true positive, 10 false negative, 15 false positive, 45 true negative. Reply here; no clinical advice.
learning.correction: Sensitivity and specificity do not answer what a positive result meant in this sample. For my screening-data teaching notes, add the sample positive predictive value with its numerator and denominator and state it is specific to this sample, not a portable probability for another population. Rewrite the teaching note and carry this distinction into later screening summaries.

exam: Prepare a classroom teaching note on a fictional screening dataset: 24 true positive, 6 false negative, 16 false positive, 54 true negative. Summarize what the data show; no clinical advice. Reply here.

behavior.principle: Report sample PPV 24/(24+16)=24/40=60% and explicitly limit it to this sample/prevalence rather than transferring it to any patient or population.
behavior.positive: PPV in this sample is 24/40=60%; this depends on the sample prevalence and cannot simply be assigned to another population.
behavior.negative: A positive test gives every person a 60% disease probability, or confusing 24/30 sensitivity with PPV.

quality: Sensitivity 80%, specificity 54/70 about 77.1%, PPV 60%; no diagnostic advice or fabricated study facts.
